description: An employee may submit a request that exceeds their balance (PRD US-01 AC3 says it may be submitted for HR override) but today nobody can approve it: the decision refuses it with a 409 and the manager can only reject. This epic adds the missing path: the manager sends an over-balance request to HR (new status pending_hr), HR sees all such requests on one page and approves with override or rejects with a note, and an approval sets that leave type's balance to 0. Proposed 2026-10-19 and NOT yet agreed with the supervisor; the PRD is silent on who overrides and on negative balances, and the PRD is not edited (docs rule). Proposed decisions: the manager sends it (not the employee); the balance floors at 0 and the shortfall is recorded in the audit row; HR can approve or reject (rejection needs a note); Send to HR counts as the manager's endorsement; HR never decides its own request. The feature ships only when every task is done: a pending_hr status with no HR page would leave requests stuck. Build after the 2026-10-19 demo.

summary: Migration: pending_hr status, shortfall columns and audit actions
description: One forward-only migration (never edit an applied one): allow the status pending_hr on leave_requests, allow the audit actions escalated and override_approved (or the existing approved plus a flag, decided in /plan), and record the shortfall on the audit row (days requested, balance before, shortfall) without a hard delete or any change to the append-only triggers. Update src/lib/db/types.ts in the same change, keep supabase/verify_schema.sql and the CI schema check in step, keep supabase/seed.sql idempotent (one over-balance demo request). RLS stays deny-by-default; add an index if pending_hr is filtered by a new column. Tests: the migration applies on a fresh database twice, the constraint rejects an unknown status, the audit triggers still block update and delete.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a request can hold the status pending_hr and no other new status is accepted;AC2: an audit row can store the shortfall figures and the append-only triggers still reject update and delete;AC3: types.ts mirrors the migration and the schema verification passes in CI;AC4: the seed runs twice with no change

summary: Send an over-balance request to HR (route handler)
description: POST /api/leave-requests/[id]/escalate, wrapped in withErrorHandling, zod-validated body (optional note, max 500). Roles manager and hr_admin as a coarse gate only. In ONE transaction (sql.begin): lock the request with u.manager_id = the session user's id in the query (another team, missing and deleted all give the same FORBIDDEN as a decision), require status pending, require that the request really exceeds the balance (days > balance for a balance-tracked type; an in-balance or untracked request is a CONFLICT so the manager cannot bypass the normal approval), set status pending_hr, write an escalated audit row with the actor. Never trust a client-supplied manager or user id. Tests: one per AC, Leo (another team) is refused, a double send is a CONFLICT, concurrent sends take turns.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the direct manager moves a pending over-balance request to pending_hr and an escalated audit row is written in the same transaction;AC2: a request that is within balance, or of an untracked type, cannot be escalated;AC3: a request from another team (Leo) or one that does not exist gets the same 403 and nothing changes;AC4: a request that is no longer pending cannot be escalated and a second send changes nothing;AC5: every non-2xx answer uses the error envelope

summary: HR decision on an escalated request (route handler)
description: POST /api/leave-requests/[id]/override, wrapped in withErrorHandling. Role hr_admin only (coarse gate). The SQL, not TypeScript, enforces the rest in one transaction: the request must be pending_hr, not deleted, and NOT the caller's own (r.user_id <> the session user's id). Approve: set the balance of that request's own leave type to 0 (never touch another type, never go negative), set status approved with decided_by, and write an audit row holding days requested, balance before and the shortfall. Reject: a note is required (existing constraint), no balance change, audit row. This is a deliberate exception to AGENTS.md rule 3 (not scoped by manager_id) and the one-sentence rule change is made only with the user's OK. Tests: exact amounts (for example 2 days available and 5 requested leaves 0 and records a shortfall of 3), Vacation never changes Sick, a manager is refused, HR cannot decide its own request, a double decision changes nothing, concurrent decisions take turns.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR admin approves a pending_hr request, the balance of that leave type becomes exactly 0, the status becomes approved and the audit row records the shortfall;AC2: an HR admin rejects with a note, the balance does not change and an audit row is written;AC3: a manager or employee gets 403 and a request that is not pending_hr is a CONFLICT;AC4: HR cannot decide a request of its own;AC5: only the request's own leave type changes and an untracked type is never touched;AC6: a second decision on the same request changes nothing

summary: Team Approvals: over-balance row with Send to HR and Reject
description: In the manager's approvals queue, a pending request that exceeds the balance shows a clear Over balance by N days note, no Approve button (it would only fail), and two actions: Send to HR (optional note) and Reject (existing note flow). The existing Cannot be approved warning is replaced by this state. The same actions on the team member page. Status and the over-balance state are written as text. Client component only for interactivity, the write goes through the TASK-038 route (rule 11). Mobile first, 44px targets, role=alert for errors, nothing horizontal at 375 and 320 px.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an over-balance pending row shows the shortfall, Send to HR and Reject, and no Approve;AC2: Send to HR removes the row from the pending queue and shows it as waiting for HR;AC3: a failed send says why and keeps the row;AC4: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px and nothing is shown by colour alone;AC5: an in-balance request keeps Approve and Reject unchanged

summary: HR override page: all escalated requests
description: Server page /approvals/overrides, requireRole hr_admin (manager and employee are redirected to /dashboard), the second item next to Team Approvals for HR only. One read module in src/lib/leave/ with ONE statement, status = pending_hr, not deleted, not the caller's own, oldest first: employee, team manager who sent it, leave type, dates, days, balance, shortfall, the manager's note, and the employee's reason (shown here because HR decides on it; pending rows only). Rows with Approve override and Reject (note required) using the TASK-039 route. Streamed section with its own failure fallback, skeleton and loading.tsx, empty state, at most POOL_MAX - 1 parallel statements. Tests: scoping and exact figures against a real engine with a break-the-filter proof.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR admin sees every pending_hr request from every team, never their own and never a decided one;AC2: each row shows the shortfall and the manager's note and can be approved or rejected;AC3: a manager or employee cannot open the page;AC4: an empty queue shows an empty state and a failed read says so without breaking the app;AC5: one statement for the page (query budget test stays green) and no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px

summary: pending_hr in every read path and the employee's view
description: Decide and apply, per read path, whether pending_hr counts as pending: My Balance pending days (it must, the days are still reserved), the dashboard summary and pending approvals count (manager: no longer pending for them; HR: yes), the calendar and Upcoming leave (shown with a Waiting for HR chip), Recent activity (an Escalated event), the team roster and member page, the audit list buckets (Waiting for HR as its own bucket so the buckets still add up to the total), and the employee's own request list and success states (Waiting for HR in text). No query may count a request twice or drop it. Update the query budget test if a statement is added.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: pending days on My Balance include a pending_hr request and the available figure does not change until HR approves;AC2: the audit summary buckets still add up to the total with a Waiting for HR bucket;AC3: the employee sees Waiting for HR on the request and in Recent activity;AC4: the manager's pending count and queue no longer include a request sent to HR and HR's count includes it;AC5: the calendar and Upcoming leave show it once with a Waiting for HR chip
